results.task: I took the same picture twice and one is smaller. Will this find them? How does it tell?
results.reply:
**Will it find them?** Not in this case. The tool only finds exact copies, and your two pictures have different bytes because one is smaller.

**What the check printed:**
- I checked 3 photos.
- I found no exact copies.
- There are no extra copies in the 3 photos I checked.
- This tool only lists exact copies. It never deletes, moves or sends photos.
- Photos that only look alike need the Photo Duplicate Finder website. Nothing was deleted or moved.

**How it tells:** It gives each photo file a fingerprint (SHA-256) based on its exact contents. Two files with the same fingerprint are identical, whatever they're named. A resized or re-saved copy has different contents, so its fingerprint differs and it won't be grouped with the original.

**For your smaller copy:** Use the Photo Duplicate Finder website. It compares how the pictures look, so it can match a resized or re-saved version. It shows you each group so you can decide what to keep.

Nothing was deleted. If you decide to remove a copy, do it yourself in your Photos or Files app. I won't say which one to keep. If you want to check another folder, tell me where it is.
